questions.question: What does globalisation refer to?
options: The increasing interconnectedness of economies, cultures and populations
The closing of all national borders
questions.explanation: Globalisation is the increasing interconnectedness of the world's economies, cultures and populations.

questions.question: What does the theory of "comparative advantage" explain?
options: Why countries benefit from specialising and trading
Why all countries should be self-sufficient
questions.explanation: Comparative advantage explains why countries benefit from specialising and trading, even if one is more efficient at everything.

questions.question: Which is a common protectionist tool?
questions.explanation: Protectionism uses tools such as tariffs (taxes on imports) and quotas (limits on imports) to protect domestic industries.

questions.question: Which institution provides the rules-based framework for international trade?
options: The European Court of Human Rights
questions.explanation: The WTO provides the rules-based framework for international trade, though it faces challenges from trade wars.

questions.question: What is one argument FOR free trade?
options: Lower prices for consumers due to competition
It eliminates the need for any trade rules
questions.explanation: Free trade can lower prices, offer greater variety and promote growth, though it can harm vulnerable industries and workers.
